**Review marker: cedar-731**

**Changed files:** none. This was analysis only. I worked from the pasted snapshot and did not open any other files in the worktree. The CSS and client script I mention (`experience.css`, `depth-experience.css`, `depth-experience-client.ts`) are unread, so statements about them are inferences.

**Opportunity 1: Home hero with a clearer reservation path and legible text over the film**
- **Sources:**
  - `src/components/composition/ExperienceComposition.astro`: the `.experience-hero` block, `.hero-entry-links`, `.film-toggle` and `.film-shade`.
  - `src/design/depth-experience.css` and `src/design/experience.css`: hero styling.
  - `src/design/depth-experience-client.ts`: the film toggle behaviour.
- **Idea:**
  - Today both hero links look equal. Make "Encontrarnos en la mesa" (reservations) the primary action and "Explorar la carta" the secondary one, using only CSS in the shared files.
  - Tune `.film-shade` so the h1 and tagline hold contrast over the poster and the video.
  - Leave the markup, `data-*` attributes, media usage IDs and credits link unchanged.
- **Accessibility risks:**
  - The title and tagline sit over moving imagery. Contrast has to hold at every frame crop, including the enlarged 1280×720 source on large screens, and on the poster alone.
  - The pause button is `hidden` until JS runs. With no JS or under reduced motion, the poster must remain and the video must not autoplay. Keep the button keyboard-reachable, at least 44px, and with a visible focus ring, since the video loops past 5 seconds (WCAG 2.2.2).
  - The `↗` arrows are `aria-hidden`, which is fine. A primary/secondary style must not rely on colour alone.
  - The video is `aria-hidden` and `tabindex=-1`, so the toggle's label has to update when the state changes ("Reproducir" / "Pausar").

**Opportunity 2: Carta page, filtered-state layout and focus order**
- **Sources:**
  - `src/design/experience-refinement.css`: the `[data-collection-state=filtered]` rules.
  - `src/components/composition/ContextualModule.astro` and `ContextualImage.astro`: the menu module and its images.
  - `src/design/depth-experience-client.ts`: the filtering logic.
- **Idea:**
  - The filtered single-dish view uses an explicit photo/copy two-column grid that collapses at 760px.
  - Make it a more editorial "selected dish" detail with larger type, a clear price/allergen/fiction note, and a visible route to Tu selección.
  - Keep the four dishes, the demo-only notices and the linked credits.
- **Accessibility risks:**
  - The CSS places the photo and copy with `grid-column` and `grid-row`. Visual order must match DOM order, or keyboard and screen-reader order will diverge.
  - Filtering changes content without a page load. Announce it through a polite live region or manage focus on the result, and don't lose focus when the filtered-out items are hidden.
  - Allergen and calorie text is fictional and must stay labelled as such. Don't present it as real safety information.
  - Cover-cropped dish photos need existing `alt` text, and any new image use must pass `evaluateExperienceUsage`. Don't add images on routes that have no approved usage.

**Constraints to preserve in both:**
- `EXPERIENCE_RENDER_USE_BLOCKED` gating.
- The footer fiction and provider notices.
- The 44px nav and footer link targets.
- The `#experience-main` focus outline.
- Mobile layout at 760px and below.

**Checks:** none run by me. Codex still needs to run contrast, keyboard, reduced-motion, no-JS and mobile captures.

**Risk:** both ideas rest on the pasted snapshot, so line-level CSS details may differ from what I assumed.
